abstracts.value: We introduce a class of noninvertible topological defects in <math display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>D</mi></mstyle></mrow></math> gauge theories whose fusion rules are the higher-dimensional analogs of those of the Kramers-Wannier defect in the <math display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>D</mi></mstyle></mrow></math> critical Ising model. As in the lower-dimensional case, the presence of such noninvertible defects implies self-duality under a particular gauging of their discrete (higher-form) symmetries. Examples of theories with such a defect include SO(3) Yang-Mills (YM) at <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></math>, <math display="inline"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> SO(3) super YM, and <math display="inline"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> SU(2) super YM at <math display="inline"><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi></math>. We also introduce an analogous construction in <math display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>D</mi></mstyle></mrow></math>, and give a number of examples in Chern-Simons–matter theories.

We introduce a class of non-invertible topological defects in (3+1)d gauge theories whose fusion rules are the higher-dimensional analogs of those of the Kramers-Wannier defect in the (1+1)d critical Ising model. As in the lower-dimensional case, the presence of such non-invertible defects implies self-duality under a particular gauging of their discrete (higher-form) symmetries. Examples of theories with such a defect include SO(3) Yang-Mills (YM) at $\theta = \pi$, $\mathcal{N}=1$ SO(3) super YM, and $\mathcal{N}=4$ SU(2) super YM at $\tau = i$. We also introduce an analogous construction in (2+1)d, and give a number of examples in Chern-Simons-matter theories.
